interfaces.name: package_outline
interfaces.package: UFQFPN-32 5x5x0.55 (active) — one of three, see below
interfaces.what: THREE PACKAGES SHIP AND THE DESIGN DOES NOT SAY WHICH. ST's own product page lists: 'UFQFPN 32 5x5x0.55 mm' (Active), 'VFQFPN 5X5X1 32L WETTABLE FLANKS' (NRND — not recommended for new design) and 'WLCSP 36B DIE3916 P05 MM' (Active). The body_mm on this row is the ACTIVE 32-pin UFQFPN, 5.0000 x 5.0000 x 0.5500 mm; the NRND VFQFPN shares its 5.0000 x 5.0000 footprint at 1.0000 mm tall, and the WLCSP36 is a different part entirely. THE FRAME IS VALID FOR ALL THREE: it is the package's geometric centre ON THE SEATING PLANE (z = 0 is the PCB land plane, +z into the body), which does not move between package options. What does move is the height (0.5500 vs 1.0000 mm) and the land pattern, and those stay CANNOT DETERMINE until the board says which is fitted. What settles it: Pollen's Robot HAT / imu_to_dxl board files (unpublished — COMPARISON.html finding 6), or a photograph of the fitted part. `accepts` is EMPTY on purpose: an SMT land joint is connection:solder-smt, which is NOT on this shelf — naming it would dangle.
interfaces.source: READ OFF THE VENDOR'S OWN PRODUCT PAGE: STMicroelectronics ST25R3916 product page https://www.st.com/en/nfc/st25r3916.html, package list and lifecycle badges, fetched 2026-09-02 (lane T). This is the vendor's page, not a distributor's transcription; it is a WEAKER source than the mechanical drawing in the ST25R3916 datasheet's package-information section, which is what would carry the land pattern and the pin-1 datum, and the row says so. That datasheet is not on disk in this folder.

interfaces.name: pcb_land
interfaces.why: the solder face of the VFQFPN32 5x5 mm package (or UFQFPN32 / WLCSP36 — the member is not chosen). No STEP or footprint fetched or measured; datasheet.pdf §6 carries the package drawings (Table 134 VFQFPN32 mechanical data) and nothing here has read a millimetre off them. A named refusal, not an empty list.

interfaces.name: antenna_1
interfaces.why: the first of the two single-ended antenna drives the sheet names ('Possibility to drive two independent single ended antennas', p.1). An antenna is a PCB or flex structure whose geometry this shelf does not have; the Microduck's head/beak antenna geometry is CANNOT DETERMINE (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §8).
